headline: Junior Court Clerk Requests Independent Review Committee After Getting A 3-Star Rating For His Lunch-Time Samosas
body:
Following recent judicial observations regarding the necessity of public accountability, Rameshwar Dayal, a Grade-IV clerk at a district court, has formally petitioned for an independent, three-member commission to investigate the 'unjust and unsubstantiated' 3-star rating he received on the office cafeteria’s internal feedback app for his homemade samosas.

Dayal, who has been bringing lunch to the court premises for seventeen years, argued that if the highest institutions of the land are subject to public scrutiny, his culinary contributions should be no different. 'The feedback mentioned that my chutney-to-potato ratio was legally insufficient, and that the crust had a structural integrity issue that bordered on negligence,' Dayal stated during a press briefing held in the breakroom. 'I am merely asking for the right to respond to these allegations of sogginess in a fair and transparent forum.'

Legal experts are divided on whether the clerk’s petition will reach a higher forum, but the clerk remains resolute. He has already begun preparing a 400-page affidavit detailing the supply chain of his spices, emphasizing that transparency in one's frying technique is a foundational principle of a functional pantry. 'If I cannot be held accountable for the crispiness of my snack, then who can?' he asked, while filing a request for a stay order on any further criticism of his lunch until the matter is heard by a specialized subcommittee on snack-based accountability.
caption: Accountability begins in the canteen. Rameshwar Dayal is leading the charge for total transparency in his lunch hour. #JudicialTransparency #SamosaScrutiny #WorkplaceDrama #OfficeLife (satire)
igHook: Would you want an independent commission reviewing your lunch decisions?
imagePrompt: A close-up of a stainless steel office canteen counter with a plastic feedback tablet showing a 3-star rating, blurred legal books in the background.

sourceHeadline.title: Judiciary cannot be beyond scrutiny, criticism necessary for accountability: CJI Surya Kant

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 is the strongest entry because it anchors its absurdity in a highly specific, low-stakes domestic detail (a samosa chutney-to-potato ratio) that feels grounded in real office dynamics. It avoids the AI-slop tendency of repeating the headline or relying on tired 'emoji' or 'shredder' tropes, maintaining a deadpan, bureaucratic tone that is both funny and oddly warm.
